name: Curiass
summary: The fleet’s dedicated lunar lander — a vacuum-only descent/ascent vehicle that the EX-4 ferry hands off to at a lunar-orbit node. Sized for the common 5 t surface-delivery job.
description: GX-04 Curiass is the fleet’s dedicated lunar lander — the vehicle the EX-4 Galahad ferry hands off to at a Luna-configuration MX-79 node in lunar orbit. It descends to the surface, performs the mission, and ascends back to the node; the EX-4 never lands. A compact, vacuum-only descent/ascent vehicle that never touches Earth.

components.name: Elongated octagon body
components.what: Longer than wide; module on each long side
components.detail: Walls slant up/in to a top docking port.

components.name: 4 corner tanks + 4 landing thrusters
components.what: Precise landing control at the widest points
components.detail: Cylindrical tanks (wider than tall), one thruster atop each — max control moment arm.

components.name: 6 legs
components.detail: Outriggers give tip-over stability on the long axis on sloped regolith.

components.name: Top docking port
components.detail: Front trapezoid window + slit side-windows; rear ladder down.

capabilities.name: Surface cargo drop (baseline)
capabilities.detail: Deliver a 5 t module to the surface (one EX-3 5 t slot) and return crew + ~0.5 t. ~27 t wet, ~2 tanker runs to fuel.

capabilities.name: Heavy drop (max)
capabilities.detail: 10 t to surface ~37 t wet — out of the common-job baseline; two trips or a different path.

modules.name: 5 t surface module
modules.purpose: Base element / cargo delivered to the Moon

calculations.title: Common-job sizing (5 t drop)
calculations.method: Descent (~1,900 m/s w/ cargo) + ascent (~1,900 m/s light), storable Isp ~316.
calculations.result: Descent prop ~12.5 t, ascent ~4.5 t → ~17 t total; wet at node ~27 t; dry ~4.4 t.
calculations.note: Sized for the common job to minimise tanker runs, not the 10 t maximum.

calculations.title: Correction to old numbers
calculations.method: Check the old mini-blueprint (dry 4.0 / wet 15.7 / 10 t / 3,800 m/s).
calculations.result: Those never closed simultaneously — 15.7 t wet gives only ~355 m/s with 10 t aboard. The 10 t was the bay ceiling, not a per-mission requirement.
calculations.note: Return mass is always small (crew + samples ~0.5–1 t); delivered-down mass sizes the vehicle.

blueprint.frame: Elongated octagon planform (longer than wide); EX-sized module on each long side.
blueprint.stations: 4 corner tanks + thrusters; central OMS bottom-center; 6 legs (4 corner + 2 outrigger); top docking port; front window; rear ladder.
blueprint.notes: Parks cold on the surface — storable propellant, no boiloff.

sections.heading: Fleet fit
sections.body: EX-4 ferries crew and modules Earth–LEO–lunar orbit; the Curiass takes them the last leg to the surface and back. Both run storable propellant fuelled at the same node, so the logistics chain is single-supply.

changelog.what: Promoted from EX-4 mini-blueprint to own vehicle sheet; sized for 5 t common job
changelog.why: Old placeholder numbers never closed; the common-job sizing is honest and minimises tanker runs.

changelog.what: 1 descent engine → 4 corner thrusters + central OMS
changelog.why: Precise landing control; adds only ~300–450 kg dry, still closes.

decisions.why: Fewer tanker runs per mission; the rare 10 t monolith is a two-trip job.
Parks cold on the lunar surface between missions — no cryogenic boiloff.

openItems: CoM shift when the 5 t cargo releases on the surface (affects ascent trim).
